rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: RAN `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/run-the-first-experiment.md` BEFORE any fix -> 'oversized: 1', '⚠ ...:68 [285w] ## Pre-reads before Module 5', exit 1. The maintainer block already carried an intended accept-note ('Slide size accepted, same argument as `getting-going.md`'s reading list:'), but it did not match the checker's required regex `^\*\*Slide size accepted:\*\*\s*(.+?)\s*(?:—|--)\s` — confirmed by running that exact regex against the file: zero matches. Two defects: the bold span read 'Slide size accepted, same argument as...' (extra clause before the colon) instead of the exact `**Slide size accepted:**` token, and it sat mid-paragraph rather than at the start of a maintainer-block line. Net effect: the checker treated the 285-word slide as UNACCEPTED and would fail any gate that runs this script (exit 1), while the maintainer block read as though it had already been handled — a silent gap between stated intent and mechanical enforcement, exactly the alarm-fatigue harm this rule's exact-format requirement exists to prevent. FIXED this session (internal maintainer-block file, plainly-wrong format, no content/decision change): split the note into its own paragraph reading `**Slide size accepted:** Pre-reads before Module 5 — same argument as ...`, mirroring the working pattern already in `getting-going.md:96`. RE-RAN after the fix: 'oversized: 0', '✓ every slide is within limits', exit 0; --report shows the slide marked `~` (accepted) at 285w. body_sha above is taken after this fix.
